testcase: Oracle .NET generation config gives conflicting emitter errors
query:
title: Oracle .NET generation config gives conflicting emitter errors

question: Hi, after rebasing our Oracle Database stable-version spec PR, .NET generation started failing. We originally had @azure-typespec/http-client-csharp-mgmt configured. The first error said Rule FlavorAzure failed and asked for options.@azure-tools/typespec-csharp.flavor: azure, so I added that block as well. Now SdkTspConfigValidation says projects must not use the legacy @azure-tools/typespec-csharp emitter. Any suggestion on how to resolve these errors?
ground_truth: For this migrated management-plane project, restore the C# config to the supported @azure-typespec/http-client-csharp-mgmt block, including the package namespace and emitter output path. Remove the deprecated @azure-tools/typespec-csharp block instead of keeping both to satisfy conflicting diagnostics. Verify supported options against the pinned management emitter, rerun TypeSpec config validation and generation, and inspect the diff. Do not substitute the data-plane emitter for this ARM SDK or assume that the first diagnostic proves legacy config is required.

testcase: Pin NetworkCloud generation while using the latest spec fixes
query:
title: Pin NetworkCloud generation while using the latest spec fixes

question: Hi, I validated the NetworkCloud client.tsp changes locally with LocalSpecRepo and the new Patch property names are generating as expected. One issue is that the latest specs checkout also picks up 2026-08-01-preview, while this SDK PR is for 2026-07-01. Go supports selecting an API version during generation. Is there an equivalent way to pin the C# generation to 2026-07-01 while still having the latest spec fixes? Does that go in the specs repo?
ground_truth: Set the documented api-version option to 2026-07-01 under @azure-typespec/http-client-csharp-mgmt in the spec project's tspconfig.yaml, not under another language's or an older C# emitter's block. Regenerate with the intended spec revision and verify that the output uses 2026-07-01 while retaining the client.tsp fixes. Coordinate and merge this spec configuration with the other spec changes; the pin affects subsequent generation and must be removed or updated when intentionally generating a later API version. Do not edit generated API-version constants as the lasting fix.

testcase: Relationships model changes break samples and need regeneration
query:
title: Relationships model changes break samples and need regeneration

question: Hi team, can I get help with the failing checks in our Relationships SDK PR? The new stable API replaced ServiceGroupMemberRelationshipProperties with ServiceGroupMemberRelationshipPropertiesV2, and the sample files are failing. Can we modify the samples directly to use the new types? I also created a spec PR to address the review comments about naming the new classes. What do I need to update in the SDK PR for those fixes?
ground_truth: Update the hand-maintained samples to the intended current SDK API; these samples are not regenerated by SDK generation. For the naming review fixes, regenerate the SDK using the spec commit containing the fixes so reviewers can verify their SDK effect, rather than only changing the spec or generated C# manually. After the spec fix merges, update tsp-location.yaml to the intended main revision and regenerate. Inspect the generated API and build samples/tests. Copilot can help using the management-specific mgmt-review-comment-resolution skill in an appropriate checkout; link its instructions and explain what to ask Copilot to do. Verify the resulting sample and generated-code fixes before re-review.

testcase: NetworkCloud breaking-change suppression remains after regeneration
query:
title: NetworkCloud breaking-change suppression remains after regeneration

question: Hi, I merged the latest main into the NetworkCloud SDK branch and regenerated, but the review still says the PR has suppressed breaking changes. The github-actions comment points to eng/apicompatbaselines/Azure.ResourceManager.NetworkCloud.xml, which I added earlier in this PR. Is that causing the issue, and is it safe to remove it? How should I handle the breaking changes?
ground_truth: The suppression introduced in this PR should not stand in for mitigating the breaking changes. Inspect its ApiCompat diagnostics and the previous GA contract, remove this newly added suppression as part of properly addressing those breaks, and verify the result with regeneration and compatibility checks. Do not generalize this to deleting unrelated existing baselines. Recommend Copilot with the management-specific mitigate-breaking-changes skill and link the instructions. Preserve required released members through supported spec or SDK customizations. Choose exact mitigations from the actual diagnostics, not from a blanket suppression rule.

testcase: Does a field-casing change break the .NET SDK?
query:
title: Does a field-casing change break the .NET SDK?

question: I want to confirm the best way to check whether changing a field's case will be a breaking change in the .NET SDK. CI passes, and I specified clientName(name) for .NET. I checked APIView and don't see a diff for this change. I'm a bit surprised because I thought something would need to change for the field to deserialize differently from the wire. Am I misunderstanding what that diff shows?
ground_truth: APIView shows changes in the public .NET contract, not every generated file or serialization implementation. A field's wire casing can change while clientName or normal C# naming keeps the public member unchanged. Compare the generated APIView with the previous GA and use ApiCompat for public compatibility; neither alone establishes wire compatibility. Generate from the changed spec and inspect the actual serialization/deserialization diff, using focused tests to verify intended wire behavior. Do not conclude that an empty APIView diff means no generated code changed or that all runtime behavior is unchanged.

testcase: Generated C# method remains after adding CodeGenSuppress
query:
title: Generated C# method remains after adding CodeGenSuppress

question: Hi, I added a custom replacement for a generated C# SDK method and used CodeGenSuppress to suppress the original. The generated method is still there, though, and the build fails with CS0111 because both methods have the same signature. What should I check to get the suppression applied without editing the generated files?
ground_truth: CodeGenSuppress is consumed during SDK code generation; adding the attribute alone does not remove an existing generated method. Check whether generation ran after the customization was added and rerun it with that customization included. Do not assume generation was skipped without checking. If the generated method remains, verify that the suppression targets the exact method name and ordered parameter types. Inspect the regenerated diff and rebuild to confirm the intended custom replacement remains without a duplicate generated method. Do not delete or patch generated files as the lasting fix, or conclude that a generator defect is the cause from this symptom alone.
